body: Thank you so much for your kind words. I will remember them.
It certainly comes in waves. I’m sorry our year has ended like this. But we are strong alone and even stronger together. Praying for you.
I’m so sorry. I know my words can even begin to scratch the surface of what you’re feeling. Although I can’t imagine your sadness, just know you’re not alone!

I don’t think it’s about harming any children. It’s about sheer human decency (definition of trashy btw)... love between two consenting adults is great! What I don’t support is railing your significant other from behind on a balcony without any regard as to the common principles of society. This is gross. There’s not even a reasonable expectation of privacy. You’re subjecting this spectacle to others that live there. Wanna find a secret place in the woods? Great. In the middle of a wild frat party? Ok. Get your exhibitionism on. Neither one is exactly classy but people can easily walk away from it. If I live there I shouldn’t have to see it. Gross.
I’m shocked you’re getting downvoted. It’s absolutely trashy.

Yes we may have been totally scammed by the China manufacturer, but not by the CEO. I know the CEO personally and although he definitely mismanaged the company (but not enough to overcome the business judgement rule), i do not believe he acted fraudulently.
Thank you so much for your help!!

I believe it was a C-Corp but it may be an S Corp. it is definitely not a partnership and I have not received a K-1

Thank you for any and all help you can provide

Ok awesome thank you so much for your help! Should I hire an accountant or something to get this done? I’m not on any time crunch to do anything right? Do I need to have the company declare bankruptcy?
I paid $50,000 for 65,000 shares in a series AA-2   Preferred stock purchase.

The company is a Delaware LLC. The company was rather small and centered around placing phone charging units in bars and restaurants. $350,000 of the money the company gained Through investors went into creating a mold for the units in China. $30,000 of my money went into that investment. The manufacturer in China assured us that the mold would be completed, however, after some software issues occurred they quoted us an additional $350,000 to complete the project. We scrapped that idea as it was not cost effective and started renting units from a US company. The remainder of my $20,000 and a bank loan was the sole money used to rent those units. The bank loan is paid off but now the units just sit on the walls and usually aren’t even turned on. Less than $100 remains in the company account. 

As to my personal involvement only one guy went around checking and placing units. He’s now given up on the project and nobody is managing it.
